title: Rabbi Abba bar Ilai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: At the end of [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.9.5.16) and in [Taanit 3:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Taanit.3.9.2), Rabbi Berekhya, Rabbi Chelbo and Rabbi Abba bar Ilai speak in the name of Rav: “Until there is no more dai”—until your lips wear out from saying dai, “enough.” [Shabbat 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.32b.8) attributes this to Rami bar Rav speaking in the name of Rav; the end of [Vayikra Rabbah, chapter 35](https://www.sefaria.org/Vayikra_Rabbah.35.12), has Rabbi Abba bar Kahana speaking in the name of Rav. Mishpachot Soferim, page 94, cites Lekach Tov on Bereshit 2:18 as Rabbi Abba bar Ila. Hyman criticizes its author for overlooking that the name there is Rava bar Ulla: the source is [Yevamot 62b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.62b.15), where Rava bar Ulla says that living without a wife means living without peace. [Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 4:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Rosh_Hashanah.4.10.2) has Rabbi Zeira and Rabbi Abba bar Ilai speaking in the name of Rav: the teruah must proceed from a plain blast.[^1]

notes.text: The consulted Jerusalem Berakhot and Taanit give Rav Abba bar Ilai in the chain. Shabbat shows Rav as the supplied patronymic and Chama as the bracketed reading for Rami. Vayikra Rabbah gives Rabbi Abba bar Kahana. Hyman’s Lekach Tov correction relies in part on the parallel in Yevamot, where Rava bar Ulla adds “without peace.”
